ai.title: AI features (optional)
ai.description: Passbox works fully without AI. If you want, a model of your choice can help with some tasks. Passwords and other secrets never go to a model.
ai.enableDescription: Off by default. Only the features you switch on below use the model, and each says exactly what it sends. These settings apply to this browser.
ai.location.on-device.description: The browser's built-in model (leave the address empty), or a model server on this computer such as Ollama. Nothing leaves this device.
ai.location.self-hosted.description: A server you or your organization runs, for example Ollama, vLLM or LocalAI, with an OpenAI-compatible interface.
ai.location.cloud.description: A provider you choose, with your own API key, for example a provider in the EU. Data goes to that provider.
ai.where.browser: the browser's built-in model on this device
ai.endpoint.hint: The base address that ends before /chat/completions, for example http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama.
ai.endpoint.browserReady: The browser's built-in model is available. To use Ollama on this computer instead, enter http://localhost:11434/v1.
ai.endpoint.browserMissing: This browser has no built-in model. Enter the address of a model server on this computer, for example http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama.
ai.problem.missing: Enter the address of the model server.
ai.problem.scheme: The address must start with https:// (or http:// for a server in your own network).
ai.problem.credentials: Enter the address without a user name or password. Put the API key in a vault item instead.
ai.problem.cloud_https: Cloud providers need an encrypted connection: use an address that starts with https://.
ai.problem.http_not_local: http:// is only allowed for servers in your own network (localhost, private addresses, .local). Use https://.
ai.problem.on_device_local: A model on this device runs on localhost. For another computer, choose “Your own server”.
ai.problem.model_missing: Enter the name of the model, as the server lists it.
ai.problem.key_missing: Choose the vault item that holds the API key.
ai.model.hint: For example llama3.2 or mistral-small-latest. Small models are enough for these features.
ai.apiKey.hint: Passbox uses the item's password (or first hidden field) only to sign in to the provider. It is never part of what the model reads.
ai.apiKey.gone: The chosen item no longer exists. Choose another one.
ai.jurisdiction: Country or region of the provider
ai.jurisdiction.hint: Shown when you switch on a feature, so you can see where the data goes.
ai.cors: The server must accept requests from {origin}. For Ollama, start it with OLLAMA_ORIGINS set to this address.
ai.featuresDescription: Each feature has its own switch. Without AI, Passbox uses rules on this device instead.
ai.feature.import-mapping: Import: suggest how columns are assigned
ai.feature.import-mapping.sends: Sends column names and patterns of the values (for example “looks like a web address”, lengths). Never the values themselves.
ai.feature.security-copilot.sends: Sends the kinds and number of findings and the affected website domains (to cloud providers as “Site A”, “Site B”). Never passwords.
ai.completeFirst: Complete the settings above to switch on a feature.
ai.log.description: Every request to a model, on this device: when, which feature, where, which kind of data and how much. The content is not kept.
ai.cloudConfirm.title: Send data to a cloud provider?
ai.cloudConfirm.text: This feature will send data to {host} ({jurisdiction}). The provider's terms decide how long it is kept.
ai.import.unknown: {count, plural, one {Passbox did not recognize # column.} other {Passbox did not recognize # columns.}}
ai.import.sendsAi: Suggestions come from {where}. Only column names and value patterns are sent, never values.
ai.import.sendsNothing: Suggestions come from value patterns on this device. AI suggestions can be switched on in Settings → AI features.
ai.import.none: No better assignment found. Choose the fields yourself.
ai.import.doneAi: {count, plural, one {Suggested a field for # column.} other {Suggested fields for # columns.}} Check them before you continue.
ai.import.donePatterns: {count, plural, one {Suggested a field for # column from its values.} other {Suggested fields for # columns from their values.}} Check them before you continue.
ai.import.failed: The AI model could not be used, so the suggestions come from value patterns.
ai.plan.title: Your plan
ai.plan.description: The most important steps first. Email and bank accounts come before the rest, because they open other accounts.
ai.plan.breached.title: {count, plural, one {Change # password found in data breaches} other {Change # passwords found in data breaches}}
ai.plan.breached.detail: Attackers try these passwords first. Change them now and let Passbox create new ones.
ai.plan.reused.title: {count, plural, one {Give # login its own password} other {Give # logins their own passwords}}
ai.plan.reused.detail: If one of these websites is hacked, attackers can get into the others too. Start with email and bank accounts.
ai.plan.weak.title: {count, plural, one {Replace # password that is easy to guess} other {Replace # passwords that are easy to guess}}
ai.plan.weak.detail: Change it on the website and let Passbox create a strong one.
ai.plan.insecure-url.title: {count, plural, one {Check # website without encryption} other {Check # websites without encryption}}
ai.plan.insecure-url.detail: These addresses start with http://. Try whether the website also works with https:// and update the address.
ai.plan.no-totp.title: {count, plural, one {Turn on two-factor sign-in for # important account} other {Turn on two-factor sign-in for # important accounts}}
ai.plan.no-totp.detail: A second step protects the account even if the password leaks. Store the key in Passbox.
ai.plan.byAi: Explained by {where} from the kinds and number of findings. Check the steps before you act; Passbox changes nothing on its own.
ai.plan.failed: The AI model could not be used. This plan comes from rules on this device.
ai.plan.byRulesAiReady: Plan from rules on this device. “Explain with AI” asks {where}.
ai.plan.byRules: Plan from rules on this device. No data was sent anywhere.
